doc.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Bostic, Washington clubs and arriving in New York
title: Later Washington gigs at Jimmy McPhail's and the Caverns
summary: Cobb recalls playing Jimmy McPhail's with Wynton Kelly and Jimmy Garrison, and the Bohemian Caverns.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What about off of U Street? What about in northeast or southwest? Like Bruce Wall’s. Was that a fixture?
I don’t remember Bruce Wall’s. I don’t remember too many places in – what was in northeast?
I never spent a lot of time that way. The only thing I even know vaguely out there was Phil what’s-his-name’s club. That’s way later. The singer?
Oh, you’re talking about on Benner Road? Jimmy. The Gold Room?

Jimmy McPhail. That’s where he lived. We went there once, because he wanted the trio, me and Wynton and – actually, it was Jimmy what’s-his-name. Used to work with Coltrane, because Paul [Chambers] had died by that time. It was Jimmy . . .

Jimmy Garrison. Me and him and Jimmy Garrison. We worked in Jimmy McPhail’s for a week or so, I think. And there was the Caverns. We worked down there for Tony, a couple times, when it was Bohemian Caverns.
Yeah. What else? There’s not too many other places.
